title: Data Type Conversions 🔄
description: Convert columns to the right types: numbers, strings, dates.

slides.title: Why Data Types Matter ⚙️
slides.content:
# Correct Types = Correct Operations

If a numeric column is stored as strings, you can’t compute the mean. If a date is stored as a string, you can’t extract the year. Pandas provides methods to convert types safely.

Common conversions:
- `to_numeric()` – string → int/float
- `to_datetime()` – string → datetime
- `astype()` – general type conversion

slides.title: The Problem: Wrong Types
slides.content: Data often arrives as object (string) type:
slides.codeSnippet:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Price': ['10.5', '20.3', 'invalid', '15.0'],
    'Date': ['2023-01-01', '2023-02-15', '2023-03-10', '2023-04-20']
})
print('Data types:')
print(df.dtypes)

slides.title: Convert to Numeric 🔢
slides.content:
## `pd.to_numeric()`

Converts a column to numeric type. If any value can’t be converted, you can handle it with the `errors` parameter:

- `errors='raise'` (default) – stops on error.
- `errors='coerce'` – invalid values become `NaN`.
- `errors='ignore'` – returns the original column unchanged.

```python
df['Price'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Price'], errors='coerce')
```

slides.title: Numeric Conversion
slides.content: Convert the Price column, coercing errors:
slides.codeSnippet:
df['Price'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Price'], errors='coerce')
print('After conversion:')
print(df)
print('\nDtypes:')
print(df.dtypes)

quizData.question: What happens to 'invalid' when using `pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce')`?

slides.title: Convert to DateTime 📅
slides.content:
## `pd.to_datetime()`

Converts a column to datetime64. Similar `errors` parameter.

- `pd.to_datetime(df['Date'])`
- `pd.to_datetime(df['Date'], format='%Y-%m-%d')` (specify format for speed)

After conversion, you get access to the `.dt` accessor:
```python
df['Date'].dt.year
df['Date'].dt.month
```

slides.title: Date Conversion
slides.codeSnippet:
df['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Date'])
print('Date dtype:', df['Date'].dtype)
df['Year'] = df['Date'].dt.year
print(df)

quizData.question: Which accessor gives the month number from a datetime column 'dt_col'?
quizData.explanation: The `.dt` accessor provides datetime properties like month, year, day.

slides.title: General Type Conversion with `astype()` 🏭
slides.content:
## `astype(dtype)`

For simpler conversions when the data is already compatible:

```python
df['ID'] = df['ID'].astype(int)
df['Category'] = df['Category'].astype('category')
```

Using `category` type for columns with few unique values saves memory and speeds up operations.

```python
df['Category'].astype('category')
```

slides.title: Astype Examples
slides.codeSnippet:
df2 = pd.DataFrame({'Grade': ['A','B','A','C','B']})
df2['Grade'] = df2['Grade'].astype('category')
print(df2['Grade'].dtype)
print(df2['Grade'].cat.categories)

slides.title: Watch Out ⚠️
slides.content:
## `astype(int)` on NaN

You cannot convert NaN to integer using `astype(int)`. Use the nullable integer type `Int64` (capital I): `df['col'].astype('Int64')`.

slides.content:
